title: Suffix copying by the split emitter
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $w,s,r$ be Boolean words, and let $q$ be any prefix and $o$ any output word. If $w=q r$, then starting the split emitter on input $w$ in state $3$ of its four states, with the first work tape containing $s$ and head position $h$, its scratch tape in the prescribed unary configuration, and output $o$, after $|r|+1$ steps it is in the configuration with no state, input head at position $|w|+1$, the same work tapes and head positions, and output $o r$.
replaced:
If the native input splits as $w = p r$, then from the split emitter's copy
state at position $\abs{p}$ with prior output $o$, exactly $\abs{r}+1$ steps
copy $r$ to the output and halt, preserving all work tapes; this includes the
empty suffix with its final blank-reading halt.
